title: Blood-thinning drug limits cartilage damage and relieves osteoarthritis pain | New Scientist
description: A study in animals suggests a drug used to thin blood might eventually be able to slow down the development of osteoarthritis. Currently, there are no approved drugs capable of doing this
author: Carissa Wong

title: Who will step up to preserve space age artefacts for future generations? | New Scientist
description: We remember 19th-century captains of industry like Andrew Carnegie because they funded vast cultural institutions. Will the Elon Musks and Jeff Bezoses of our time do the same to preserve humanity’s spacefaring legacy?
author: New Scientist

title: Arguments over finance dominate COP climate talks once again | New Scientist
description: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has got off to a chaotic start and a familiar dispute over who should pay for tackling climate change is already emerging as the biggest obstacle to progress
author: Manuela Callari

title: X aims to safely land Starship and booster stage after orbital flight | New Scientist
description: The upcoming Starship test flight is the most ambitious to date and, if successful, will mark an important milestone in the company's mission to create a truly reusable launch vehicle that dramatically lowers the cost of space launches
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Re-analysis of black hole data proves iconic ring shape really is there | New Scientist
description: The doughnut shape of the Event Horizon Telescope’s first image of a black hole has come under fire, but an independent check showed that it – and general relativity – still stands
author: Leah Crane

title: Revised approach for assessing obesity improves on BMI | New Scientist
description: Using data from more than 800,000 people, researchers have tested a system that can identify those with obesity who would benefit from treatment, and those who don't require intervention
author: Starre Vartan
